newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent surges on late short-covering, technical.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent surges on late short-covering, technical.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed strongly on Thursday, surging to post a new session high in late trade as a wave of short-covering sparked technical buy orders, dealers said.
Jan Brent closed at $24.64 a barrel, up 85 cents and fewer than 50 cents below the October 15 post-Gulf War high of $25.06.
Traders said the prospect of more strikes by French refinery workers provided the initial spur, lifting Jan Brent through $24.30 a barrel, catching independent floor traders short.
"The locals thought this morning's rally was topping out and when it moved up again they had to get out," said a broker.
"Shorting this market is a very dangerous game," he added.
France's largest union said late Thursday it would recommend striking Elf refinery workers keep up their action after concessions on pay failed to address concerns over job cuts.

The eight-day strike, which has shut in a quarter of the country's refining capacity and could spread to other companies next week, comes at a time of historically low stocks of heating oil and gasoline in the U.S. and Europe.
Any sign of a sustained disruption in supply with winter fast approaching will send prices soaring, dealers said.
"You've got to trade this from the long side," said one.
Others said Brent got a boost from hedge fund interest, drawing money out of equity markets, currencies and other commodities, in thin volume late dealing.
"We had some fund buying but apart from that it was just loads of stop (loss orders) being hit," said a broker.
Earlier, Dec IPE gas oil closed $5.50 a tonne higher at $229.75, just 75 cents off the session high.
The Dec/Jan backwardation ended 50 cents wider at $2.25 a tonne.
